```{r file description}

#This file contains all primary analyses drawing from secondary data of parents' ideological beliefs for Experiment 2. 

```

```{r upload PANDA data (s2), include = FALSE}

##Read in cleaned PANDA data file
panda_csv <- read.csv(here::here("costly_data_s2_idbeliefs.csv"), header = TRUE)
panda_csv <- panda_csv[-c(1)]

##Trim to only vars we need
panda <- panda_csv %>%
  select(ID, condition_group, age, age_c, liking_correct, q_get_to_watch, q_punish_decide, q_feel_lock, q_feel_open, q_next_time, q_person_day, q_play_with, q_feel_bad, pol_id_new, pol_id_new_c, pol_id_spouse, pol_id_combo, pol_id_combo_c, 35:40, start_date)

```

```{r secondary data for s2, include = FALSE}

##Read in secondary data from BC study
bc_raw <- read.csv(here::here("secondary_data_long.csv"), header = TRUE, na.strings = c("", "NA"))
bc <- bc_raw

##Read in BC file with adjusted dot
bc_shortdot_raw <- read.csv(here::here("secondary_data_dot.csv"), header = TRUE, na.strings = c("", "NA"))
bc_dot <- bc_shortdot_raw

#Change dot to real_dot to distinguish when merging
bc_dot <- bc_dot %>%
  rename(dot_real = dot,
         parent_survey_dot_real = parent_survey_dot)

#Clean to just what we need
bc_dot <- bc_dot %>%
  select(ID, wave, start_date, parent_survey_dot_real)

```

```{r cleaning of secondary data, include = FALSE}

#Keep only columns we need
bc_short <- bc %>%
  select(ID, valid.data, dot, parent_survey_dot, wave, ambiguous, choose1, essentialist, structural, choose2, status_high, exp_endorse_1, exp_endorse_2, exp_choice, value_priorities_1, value_priorities_2, value_priorities_7, how_often_3, how_often_7, hi_FRIENDS_6, hi_FRIENDS_7, hi_FRIENDS_8, hi_live_4, age_app_4, comfort_4, helpful_4, politics_1)

#Merge with PANDA data for Tobi
output_tobi <- left_join(panda, bc_short, by = "ID")
write.csv(output_tobi, "costly_bc_output.csv")

#Divide up into parent and kids
bc_kid <- bc_short %>%
  select(ID, valid.data, dot, wave, ambiguous, choose1, essentialist, structural, choose2, status_high)

bc_parent <- bc_short %>%
  select(ID, valid.data, parent_survey_dot, dot, wave, exp_endorse_1, exp_endorse_2, exp_choice, value_priorities_1, value_priorities_2, value_priorities_7, how_often_3, how_often_7, hi_FRIENDS_6, hi_FRIENDS_7, hi_FRIENDS_8, hi_live_4, age_app_4, comfort_4, helpful_4, politics_1)

#Create row of total NAs per kid
bc_kid$na_count<-rowSums(apply(is.na(bc_kid),2,as.numeric))

#Select rows with fewest NAs
bc_kid_min <- bc_kid %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  slice_min(na_count) 

#Create row of total NAs per parent
bc_parent$na_count<-rowSums(apply(is.na(bc_parent),2,as.numeric))

#Select rows with fewest NAs
bc_parent_min <- bc_parent %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  slice_min(na_count)

#Find out how many IDs are overlapped
length(intersect(panda$ID, bc_kid_min$ID))
length(intersect(panda$ID, bc_parent_min$ID)) 

#Merge with PANDA, keep all that are in PANDA
panda_bc_kid_all <- left_join(panda, bc_kid_min, by = "ID")
panda_bc_parent_all <- left_join(panda, bc_parent_min, by = "ID")

#Find duplicate entries in adult df
dupe_parent <- data.frame(table(panda_bc_parent_all$ID))
dupe_parent <- panda_bc_parent_all[panda_bc_parent_all$ID %in% dupe_parent$Var1[dupe_parent$Freq > 1],]
dupe_parent <- dupe_parent %>%
  select(ID, wave, start_date, exp_endorse_1, exp_endorse_2) %>%
  filter(!is.na(exp_endorse_1)) #filtering for just the dupes we care about

#Send to Tobi
output_tobi_abb <- dupe_parent
write.csv(output_tobi_abb, "costly_bc_output_short.csv")

#Select only kids from wave closest to Costly (delete kids from waves further apart; referencing bc_dot df)
panda_bc_parent_all_dot <- panda_bc_parent_all %>%
  filter(!(ID == "157H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "1580H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "1630H" & wave == "w5"),
         !(ID == "1720H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "385H" & wave == "w1"),
         !(ID == "4399H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "4512H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "4535H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "4556H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "5391H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "5527H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "5656H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "5733H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "5774H" & wave == "w3"))
         
panda_bc_kid_all_dot <- panda_bc_kid_all %>%
  filter(!(ID == "157H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "1580H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "1630H" & wave == "w5"),
         !(ID == "1720H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "385H" & wave == "w1"),
         !(ID == "4399H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "4512H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "4535H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "4556H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "5391H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "5527H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "5656H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "5733H" & wave == "w3"),
         !(ID == "5774H" & wave == "w3"))
         
#Delete duplicate entries
panda_bc_kid <- panda_bc_kid_all_dot %>%
  distinct(ID, .keep_all = TRUE)

panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent_all_dot %>%
  distinct(ID, .keep_all = TRUE)

#Check that all responses we have for relevant parent measures are in there (N = 131)
test <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  select(ID, exp_endorse_1) %>%
  filter(!is.na(exp_endorse_1))

```

```{r clean secondary kid data, include = FALSE}

#Choose1 and Choose2 (essentialist = 1, structural = 0)
panda_bc_kid <- panda_bc_kid %>%
  mutate(choose1 = case_when(
         choose1 == "essentialist" ~ 1,
         choose1 == "structural" ~ 0,
         TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA))) %>%
  mutate(choose2 = case_when(
         choose2 == "essentialist" ~ 1,
         choose2 == "structural" ~ 0,
         TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)))

panda_bc_kid <- panda_bc_kid %>%
  mutate(status_high = case_when(
         status_high == "stereotype consistent" ~ 0,
         status_high == "stereotype inconsistent" ~ 1,
         TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)))

```

```{r clean secondary parent data, include = FALSE}

#Clean parent data first

#exp_endorse_1 (essentialist reasons) and exp_endorse 2 (structural reasons) 
panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  mutate(exp_endorse_ess = case_when(
         exp_endorse_1 == "Strongly disagree" ~ 1,
         exp_endorse_1 == "Disagree" ~ 2,
         exp_endorse_1 == "Somewhat disagree" ~ 3,
         exp_endorse_1 == "Neither agree nor disagree" ~ 4,
         exp_endorse_1 == "Somewhat agree" ~ 5,
         exp_endorse_1 == "Agree" ~ 6,
         exp_endorse_1 == "Strongly agree" ~ 7,
         TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA))) %>%
  mutate(exp_endorse_struc = case_when(
         exp_endorse_2 == "Strongly disagree" ~ 1,
         exp_endorse_2 == "Disagree" ~ 2,
         exp_endorse_2 == "Somewhat disagree" ~ 3,
         exp_endorse_2 == "Neither agree nor disagree" ~ 4,
         exp_endorse_2 == "Somewhat agree" ~ 5,
         exp_endorse_2 == "Agree" ~ 6,
         exp_endorse_2 == "Strongly agree" ~ 7,
         TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)))

#Exp_choice (1 = essentialist explanation, 0 = structural explanation)
panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  mutate(exp_choice = case_when(
    exp_choice == "Due to something specific to them, such as their work ethic or financial choices." ~ 1,
    exp_choice == "Due to something about society, such as access to jobs and education." ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)))

#Values_Priorities_1 and Values_Priorities_2 (1 = most important, 8 = least important)
panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  rename(value_equality = value_priorities_1,
         value_freedom = value_priorities_2,
         value_natsec = value_priorities_7)

#How_often questions
panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  mutate(how_often_racetalk = case_when(
    how_often_3 == "Never" ~ 0,
    how_often_3 == "Rarely" ~ 1,
    how_often_3 == "Sometimes" ~ 2,
    how_often_3 == "Very Often" ~ 3,
    how_often_3 == "Often" ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA))) %>%
  mutate(how_often_culturalevent = case_when(
    how_often_7 == "Never" ~ 0,
    how_often_7 == "Rarely" ~ 1,
    how_often_7 == "Sometimes" ~ 2,
    how_often_7 == "Very Often" ~ 3,
    how_often_7 == "Often" ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)))

#How important (hi_) child's friends questions
panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  mutate(hi_friends_racediv = case_when(
    hi_FRIENDS_6 == "Not at all important" ~ 0,
    hi_FRIENDS_6 == "Slightly important" ~ 1,
    hi_FRIENDS_6 == "Moderately important" ~ 2,
    hi_FRIENDS_6 == "Very important" ~ 3,
    hi_FRIENDS_6 == "Extremely important" ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA))) %>%
  mutate(hi_friends_ecosim = case_when(
    hi_FRIENDS_7 == "Not at all important" ~ 0,
    hi_FRIENDS_7 == "Slightly important" ~ 1,
    hi_FRIENDS_7 == "Moderately important" ~ 2,
    hi_FRIENDS_7 == "Very important" ~ 3,
    hi_FRIENDS_7 == "Extremely important" ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA))) %>%
  mutate(hi_friends_polsim = case_when(
    hi_FRIENDS_8 == "Not at all important" ~ 0,
    hi_FRIENDS_8 == "Slightly important" ~ 1,
    hi_FRIENDS_8 == "Moderately important" ~ 2,
    hi_FRIENDS_8 == "Very important" ~ 3,
    hi_FRIENDS_8 == "Extremely important" ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)))

#How important (hi_) live questions
panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  mutate(hi_live_div = case_when(
    hi_live_4 == "Not at all important" ~ 0,
    hi_live_4 == "Slightly important" ~ 1,
    hi_live_4 == "Moderately important" ~ 2,
    hi_live_4 == "Very important" ~ 3,
    hi_live_4 == "Extremely important" ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)))

#How age-appropriate questions
panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  mutate(age_app_race = case_when(
    age_app_4 == "Very inappropriate" ~ 0,
    age_app_4 == "Inappropriate" ~ 1,
    age_app_4 == "In the middle" ~ 2,
    age_app_4 == "Appropriate" ~ 3,
    age_app_4 == "Very appropriate" ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)))

#How comfortable questions
panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  mutate(comfort_race = case_when(
    comfort_4 == "Very uncomfortable" ~ 0,
    comfort_4 == "Uncomfortable" ~ 1,
    comfort_4 == "In the middle" ~ 2,
    comfort_4 == "Comfortable" ~ 3,
    comfort_4 == "Very comfortable" ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)))

#How helpful questions
panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  mutate(helpful_race = case_when(
    helpful_4 == "Very unhelpful" ~ 0,
    helpful_4 == "Unhelpful" ~ 1,
    helpful_4 == "In the middle" ~ 2,
    helpful_4 == "Helpful" ~ 3,
    helpful_4 == "Very helpful" ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)))

#Politics (just to double-check with Costly political ID var)
panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  mutate(politics_bc = case_when(
    politics_1 == "Very Conservative" ~ 7,
    politics_1 == "Conservative" ~ 6,
    politics_1 == "Slightly Conservative" ~ 5,
    politics_1 == "Middle-of-the-road"~ 4,
    politics_1 == "Slightly Liberal" ~ 3,
    politics_1 == "Liberal" ~ 2,
    politics_1 == "Very Liberal" ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)))

```

```{r mean-center ideology-linked variables, include = FALSE}

#Mean-center each variable of interest
panda_bc_parent$exp_endorse_ess_c <- scale(panda_bc_parent$exp_endorse_ess, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

panda_bc_parent$exp_endorse_struc_c <- scale(panda_bc_parent$exp_endorse_struc, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

panda_bc_parent$value_freedom_c <- scale(panda_bc_parent$value_freedom, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

```

```{r run models with parent data on punishment, include = FALSE}

#Run models with BC vars from parents
punish_bc_parent1 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ exp_endorse_ess_c*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)
summary(punish_bc_parent1) #sig 2-way

punish_bc_parent2 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ exp_endorse_struc_c*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)
summary(punish_bc_parent2) #marginal 2-way

punish_bc_parent3 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ exp_choice*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)

punish_bc_parent4 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ value_equality*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)

punish_bc_parent5 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ value_freedom_c*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)

punish_bc_parent6 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ how_often_racetalk*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)
summary(punish_bc_parent6) #ns

punish_bc_parent7 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ how_often_culturalevent*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)

punish_bc_parent8 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ hi_friends_racediv*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)

punish_bc_parent9 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ hi_friends_ecosim*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)

punish_bc_parent10 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ hi_friends_polsim*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)

punish_bc_parent11 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ hi_live_div*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)

punish_bc_parent12 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ age_app_race*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)

punish_bc_parent13 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ comfort_race*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)

punish_bc_parent15 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ value_natsec*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)
```

## Distribution of new parent variables that interact with condition to predict punishment
```{r plot distributions of parent variables, include = TRUE}

hist_ess <- ggplot(data = panda_bc_parent,
                     aes(x = exp_endorse_ess)) +
              geom_histogram(color = "white", fill = "80CAA4") +
              xlab("Parents' Endorsement of Essentialist Explanations for Inequality \n (1 = Strongly Disagree, 7 = Strongly Agreee)") + 
              ylab("Number of Participants") +
              scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7)) + 
              expand_limits(x = c(1, 7)) +
              theme_classic()
hist_ess

hist_struc <- ggplot(data = panda_bc_parent,
                     aes(x = exp_endorse_struc)) +
              geom_histogram(color = "white", fill = "80CAA4") +
              xlab("Parents' Endorsement of Structural Explanations for Inequality \n (1 = Strongly Disagree, 7 = Strongly Agreee)") +

              scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7)) +
```

## Correlations of new parent variables and political ideology (as used in Costly PANDA)
```{r calculate correlations with parent ID, include = TRUE}

corr.test(panda_bc_parent$pol_id_new, panda_bc_parent$exp_endorse_ess) #r = .30, p < .001
corr.test(panda_bc_parent$pol_id_new, panda_bc_parent$exp_endorse_struc) #r = -.38, p < .001  
corr.test(panda_bc_parent$pol_id_new, panda_bc_parent$value_freedom) #r = -.15, p = .10

```

## Model 1: Predicting punishment from condition and parents' endorsement of essentialist explanations for inequality
```{r follow up on findings from parents - 1, include = TRUE}

#Model 1: endorsement of essentialist explanations for inequality (N = 128)
punish_bc_parent1 <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ exp_endorse_ess_c*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)
summary(punish_bc_parent1) #sig 2-way

punish_bc_parent1_plot <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ exp_endorse_ess*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)
summary(punish_bc_parent1_plot)

#Get predicted means for graphing
predicted_bc_parent1 <-effect("exp_endorse_ess*condition_group",
                                    mod=punish_bc_parent1_plot, confidence.level = .975)
predicted_bc_parent1<-as.data.frame(predicted_bc_parent1)

#Create labels
exp_endorse_label <- c("1 \n More Liberal \n Responding \n ('Strongly Disagree')", "2", "3", "4", "5","6", "7 \n More Conservative \n Responding \n ('Strongly Agree')")

#Plot predicted means
plot_punish_bc_parent1 <- ggplot() + 
  geom_jitter(data = panda_bc_parent, aes(x = exp_endorse_ess, y = q_punish_decide, 
                  group = condition_group, color = condition_group), alpha = .7, height = .1) +
  stat_smooth(data = predicted_bc_parent1, aes(x = exp_endorse_ess, y = fit,
                                               group = condition_group, color = condition_group),
              method = "glm", method.args =list(family="binomial"), 
              fill = "#F6F3FF",
              se = TRUE,
              size = 2) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Parents' Endorsement of \n Essentialist Explanations for Inequality",  
  y ="Decision to Enact Costly Punishment\nAgainst Transgressor",
  color = "Transgressor's\n Group") +
  scale_color_manual(
  values = c("#8C8C8C", "#1F1F1F"),
  labels = c("Ingroup", "Outgroup")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
                     labels = exp_endorse_label) + 
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0,1), labels = c("No", "Yes")) + 
  expand_limits(x = 7.5) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3.627, linetype = "dashed", size = 1.2, color = "#0E2EE4") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 3.50, y = .38, xend = 1.5, yend = .38), arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.5, "cm")), color = "#0E2EE4", size = 1.2) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
        rect = element_rect(fill = "transparent")) 
plot_punish_bc_parent1 

#Run J-N analysis

#Check simple effects (within in- and out-group)
punish_bc_parent1_simp <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group/exp_endorse_ess_c*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)
summary(punish_bc_parent1_simp) #effect of parents' essentialist explanations is in out-group

#First, change condition to numeric variable (for J-N to run)
panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  mutate(condition_num = case_when(
    condition_group == "ingroup_toogit" ~ 0,
    condition_group == "outgroup_flurp" ~ 1,
  ))

#Re-run model with numeric condition variable and with pol_id_new not centered (for interpretability of graph)
punish_bc_parent1_JN <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_num*exp_endorse_ess*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)
#summary(punish_bc_parent1_JN) 
sim_slopes(punish_bc_parent1_JN, pred="exp_endorse_ess", modx="condition_num")

#J-N analysis code from other website
jn_parent1 <- johnson_neyman(
  punish_bc_parent1_JN,
  condition_num,
  exp_endorse_ess,
  vmat = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  plot = TRUE,
  control.fdr = FALSE,
  line.thickness = 0.5,
  df = "residual",
  digits = getOption("jtools-digits", 3),
  critical.t = NULL,
  sig.color = "#00BFC4",
  insig.color = "#F8766D",
  mod.range = c(1,7),
  title = "Johnson-Neyman plot: Parents' Essentialist Endorsement"
)
jn_parent1 #effect of in-group > out-group begins at endorsement below 3.627 (~disagree that essentialist reasons explain; liberal end of spectrum); no significant out-group > in-group here

```

## Model 2: Predicting punishment from condition and parents' endorsement of structural explanations for inequality
```{r follow up on findings from parents - 2, include = TRUE}

#Model 2: endorsement of essentialist explanations for structural (N = 128)

punish_bc_parent2_plot <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ exp_endorse_struc*condition_group*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)

#Get predicted means for graphing
predicted_bc_parent2 <-effect("exp_endorse_struc*condition_group",
                                    mod=punish_bc_parent2_plot, confidence.level = .975)
predicted_bc_parent2 <-as.data.frame(predicted_bc_parent2)

#Create labels
exp_struc_label <- c("1 \n More Conservative \n Responding \n ('Strongly Disagree')", "2", "3", "4", "5","6", "7 \n More Liberal \n Responding \n ('Strongly Agree')")

#Plot predicted means
plot_punish_bc_parent2 <- ggplot() + 
  geom_jitter(data = panda_bc_parent, aes(x = exp_endorse_struc, y = q_punish_decide, 
                  group = condition_group, color = condition_group), alpha = .7, height = .1) +
  stat_smooth(data = predicted_bc_parent2, aes(x = exp_endorse_struc, y = fit,
                                               group = condition_group, color = condition_group),
              method = "glm", method.args =list(family="binomial"), 
              fill = "#F1EAFF",
              se = TRUE,
              size = 1.8) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Parents' Endorsement of \n Structural Explanations for Inequality",  
  y ="Decision to Enact Costly Punishment\nAgainst Transgressor",
  color = "Transgressor's\n Group") +
  scale_color_manual(
  values = c("#8C8C8C", "#1F1F1F"),
  labels = c("Ingroup", "Outgroup")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
                     labels = exp_endorse_label) + 
  expand_limits(x = 1) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none")
plot_punish_bc_parent2

#Check simple effects (within in- and out-group)
punish_bc_parent2_simp <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_group/exp_endorse_struc*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)
summary(punish_bc_parent2_simp) #effect of parents' structural explanations appears in out-group

#Run J-N analysis

#First, change condition to numeric variable (for J-N to run)
panda_bc_parent <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  mutate(condition_num = case_when(
    condition_group == "ingroup_toogit" ~ 0,
    condition_group == "outgroup_flurp" ~ 1,
  ))

#Re-run model with numeric condition variable and with pol_id_new not centered (for interpretability of graph)
punish_bc_parent2_JN <- glm(q_punish_decide ~ condition_num*exp_endorse_struc*age_c, family = binomial, data = panda_bc_parent)
#summary(punish_bc_parent2_JN) 

#J-N analysis code from other website
jn_parent2 <- johnson_neyman(
  punish_bc_parent2_JN,
  condition_num,
  exp_endorse_struc,
  vmat = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  plot = TRUE,
  control.fdr = FALSE,
  line.thickness = 0.5,
  df = "residual",
  digits = getOption("jtools-digits", 3),
  critical.t = NULL,
  sig.color = "#00BFC4",
  insig.color = "#F8766D",
  mod.range = c(1,7),
  title = "Johnson-Neyman plot: Parents' Structuralist Endorsement"
)
jn_parent2 #effect of in-group > out-group begins at endorsement above 5.261 (~agree that structural reasons explain; liberal end of spectrum); no significant out-group > in-group here

```

#Generate correlation table for ideology-linked vars
```{r corr tables for id-linked vars, include = TRUE}

parent_idlinked <- panda_bc_parent %>%
  select(pol_id_new, exp_endorse_ess, exp_endorse_struc_rev, value_freedom_rev)
parent_idlinked <- as.matrix(parent_idlinked)
parent_idlinked_corr <- rcorr(parent_idlinked)
parent_idlinked_corr

#Convert to df
parent_idlinked_corr_r <- as.data.frame(parent_idlinked_corr$r)
parent_idlinked_corr_r <- format(parent_idlinked_corr_r, digits = 2)

#Export corr table
write.csv(parent_idlinked_corr_r, "parent_panda_idlinked_corr.csv")
```
